# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by tools/settings/reference.py; do not edit. -->

Settings use UTF-8 YAML with `config_version: 1`. Server commands are
`/lsslod reload` or `/vsslod reload`; client commands are `/lss reload` or `/vss reload`.
Sodium Apply saves the client draft and automatically runs the same validated reload.
Direct YAML edits still require a reload command or restart. Failed saves stay inactive.

H means reload (automatic on Sodium Apply), S means the next physical client connection after an accepted
reload, and R means restart. A disk edit alone changes none of these. Invalid documents
are rejected as a whole; numeric normalization is reported without rewriting the file.

Fresh terrain radii are Overworld 512 chunks, Nether 64 chunks, End 512 chunks, and
512 chunks for other dimensions. JSON migration preserves old scalar and per-world
choices. Explicit `{}` and `[]` replace default collections, including the vanilla
dimension overrides. Paper lookup is exact world name, dimension identifier, then default.

Existing preferred-brand YAML wins; otherwise the other brand's YAML is adopted.
Only when neither exists is JSON migrated, preserving its source stem and exact-byte
backup. Migration accepts the old Gson loader's comments and lenient JSON syntax.
Migration is one-way: v0.15.x reads the retained JSON and ignores YAML edits;
copy any desired changes back into JSON before downgrading.
Invalid authoritative YAML never falls back to JSON. Reload does not write files.

Experimental client keys (`lod.source`, `lod.dh.*`, `lod.voxy_border_fill`,
`integrations.map_ingestion.nether_store_mib`, `far_players.extend_far_plane`) live in a
sidecar file beside the selected client file (`lss-client-experimental.yaml` or
`vss-client-experimental.yaml`), so the main client file stays readable by v0.16.0.
The sidecar holds only nondefault values; deleting it restores the defaults. Allow DH
Server Terrain (`lod.source: distant_horizons`) is on by default, so turning it off
writes `source: lss` to the sidecar. Older
development builds wrote these keys into the main file: they are still honoured on read
and the next save moves them into the sidecar (retired `lod.dh.refresh_seconds` and
`lod.dh.profile` are removed). One reload reads both files.

Map ingestion was renamed from `integrations.xaero_map` to `integrations.map_ingestion`
(it now covers Xaero's World Map and JourneyMap). The old group is still read and is
rewritten under the new name by the next save that changes a setting; startup never
rewrites it. New files enable map ingestion; migration from JSON keeps an absent
`enableXaeroMapBridge` off. **Downgrade exception:** LSS 0.17 and older reject the new
group, so a file created or saved by a newer build loads there only after renaming
`map_ingestion:` back to `xaero_map:` under `integrations:` (or deleting the file).

`privacy.request_no_map_ingestion` (0.19.0) is applied by a reload. **Server downgrade
exception:** LSS 0.18 and older reject unknown keys, so a server file created by a newer
build loads there only after deleting that line (or the file).

`far_players.hide_permission_holders` (0.21.0) is applied by a reload. Off (the default),
the `lss.farplayers.hidden` / `vss.farplayers.hidden` permission hides nobody by itself and
players choose with Share My Position; on, every holder is hidden, as before 0.21.0. An
upgraded file gains the key only when the setting is changed. **Server downgrade
exception:** LSS 0.20 and older reject unknown keys, so a server file that carries the
key (every file a newer build creates) loads there only after deleting that line (or the
file).

`far_players.mode` takes four values, applied by a reload: `off` (nobody is shown),
`opt_in` (only players whose own client shares their position), `on` (the default:
everyone, and a player can hide with Share My Position) and, new in 0.21.0, `required`
(everyone is shown and cannot opt out, except holders of `lss.farplayers.hidden` /
`vss.farplayers.hidden`; a player whose choice is overridden is told so once in chat).
**Server downgrade exception:** LSS 0.20 and older reject the value `required`, so a
server file that says `mode: "required"` loads there only after changing it.

```yaml
# LOD Server Support — Fabric/NeoForge server defaults.
# Edit this file, then run /lsslod reload. Settings marked [restart] wait for restart.
# Reload changes policy for new work; existing jobs/reads drain and cache trimming can lag.
# Distances are radii. 1 chunk = 16 blocks; 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes.
config_version: 1 # Local settings schema version, independent of the network protocol.

# Serves distant terrain to compatible clients beyond vanilla's view distance.
# This does not increase the server's simulation distance or keep distant chunks ticking.
service:
  enabled: true # [restart] Enable the server's LOD service.
  require_permission: false # Require both lss.use and vss.use; nodes default to allowed.
  # show_permission_refusal: true # With require_permission on, a player without the permission is
  #   told "distant terrain here needs a permission you don't have". false = they see the general
  #   "switched off here". Courtesy, not secrecy: a player can compare with a friend. Remove the
  #   first "#" to set it; version 0.22 and older do not know this setting.

# Larger radii reveal more terrain, but cover more columns and can increase
# generation, transfer, cache and disk work. Doubling a radius covers roughly four
# times the area; a large configured radius does not mean it fills instantly.
lod:
  distance:
    default_chunks: 512 # Fallback for dimensions not listed below; range 1–2048, 0 = off.
    by_dimension: # Fresh-install defaults; 0 turns LODs off in that dimension.
      "minecraft:overworld": 512 # Overworld radius in chunks.
      "minecraft:the_nether": 64 # Nether radius in chunks.
      "minecraft:the_end": 512 # End radius in chunks.

# Lets LOD requests create terrain that does not yet exist in the world.
# This costs world-generation CPU time and grows the normal world files, independently
# of the LOD store. With generation off, existing terrain can still be served.
# Higher concurrency can fill missing terrain sooner, but competes with gameplay.
generation:
  enabled: true # Generate missing terrain; disabling stops new jobs, existing jobs finish.
  concurrency:
    global: 40 # Maximum concurrent generations across the server; range 1–512.
    per_player: 40 # Maximum per player; cannot exceed the global limit.
  timeout_ticks: 1200 # New jobs only; 60 seconds at 20 TPS, longer under lag; range 20–12000.

# Limits and schedules LOD traffic so it shares resources with normal gameplay.
# Bandwidth limits count uncompressed payload work, so they also limit client decode
# work; compressed network traffic can be much smaller. Lower limits slow terrain fill.
network:
  bandwidth:
    per_player_mib_per_second: 25 # Raw MiB/s before compression; 0 clamps to 1 KiB/s, not unlimited.
    global_mib_per_second: 75 # Shared raw MiB/s budget; 0 clamps to 1 KiB/s, not unlimited.
  send_queue_limit_per_player: 1024 # Admission ceiling; lowering it lets existing work drain.
  ping_backstop: true # Reduce LOD traffic when player latency indicates congestion.
  send_pacing: true # Spread LOD sends across ticks to reduce bursts.
  yield_to_vanilla: true # Let normal game traffic take transport priority; applies next flush.

# Keeps previously downloaded terrain up to date when the world changes.
# Shorter dirty-broadcast intervals show edits sooner but can send updates more often.
# Region summaries let returning clients validate cached areas without downloading
# every column again; they describe freshness, not the terrain itself.
updates:
  # Tick-driven: 200 ticks = 10 seconds at 20 TPS, longer under lag.
  dirty_broadcast_interval_ticks: 200 # 0 disables pushes, not invalidation; otherwise 20–6000.
  region_summaries: true # Accept new region-validation requests; accepted requests can finish.

storage:
  # Reader threads and concurrent reads control pressure on world-file access.
  # More parallel reads can improve throughput, but can also compete with gameplay
  # for disk and CPU. Automatic sizing accounts for the active read path and store.
  disk:
    reader_threads: 0 # [restart] 0 = automatic; explicit range 1–64.
    max_concurrent_reads: 0 # 0 = automatic, based on the active reader pool and store.
    background_priority: true # [restart] Use background-priority reads where supported.
    split_background_reads: true # [restart] Separate background read work where supported.
  # This RAM cache holds column freshness timestamps, not complete terrain.
  # More capacity can avoid repeated timestamp lookups, at the cost of server memory.
  # Reducing capacity trims gradually; it does not clear the entire cache on reload.
  timestamp_cache_mib_per_dimension: 0 # 0 = automatic from the largest active LOD radius.
  # Briefly remembering missing columns avoids repeatedly checking unavailable terrain.
  # A longer lifetime can delay another lookup for newly available data on a memo hit.
  miss_memo_ttl_seconds: 30 # 0 disables; maximum 60. Changing this clears old miss memos.
  # Persistent cache of prepared LOD columns, reused across players and restarts.
  # Cache hits reduce repeated world-file parsing, serialization and, when the
  # client's format supports reuse, compression. Store reads still use disk I/O.
  # Tradeoff: extra disk space and writes as terrain is cached or updated. A fully
  # warmed store can be comparable in size to the region files; actual use depends
  # on the world and how much terrain has been cached. This is rebuildable data.
  # Off still allows normal LOD serving, but loses this reuse. Disabling the store
  # does not delete its existing files or reclaim their disk space.
  lod_store:
    enabled: true # [restart] Fresh installs enable this; migration preserves old behavior.
    # Smaller limits retain less prepared terrain, so evicted columns may need
    # processing again. This bounds live database data, not total filesystem use:
    # SQLite journal files and space awaiting reclamation can add overhead.
    # Lowering the cap evicts gradually; reload does not instantly free filesystem space.
    max_size_mib: 0 # 0 = unlimited; positive range 64–1,048,576 MiB.
    # Periodically recheck saved-world freshness. Save hooks already handle runtime
    # invalidation here, so this is normally off; extra sweeps can discard reusable rows.
    resweep_interval_seconds: 0 # 0 disables future periodic sweeps; an active sweep can finish.
    # Prepare cached LODs from existing world files before clients request them.
    # This shifts CPU and disk work earlier so later visitors can benefit from hits.
    # It does not generate new terrain. Higher rates finish sooner but add load;
    # gameplay/reader-pressure guards can keep the actual rate below this ceiling.
    # Disabling stops after the current column; re-enabling resumes unfinished work.
    # Manual job commands need this enabled; a rate edit does not undo a manual stop.
    backfill:
      enabled: true # Allow background backfill; inactive on Paper/Folia.
      columns_per_second: 500 # Ceiling for the running job; range 10–1000.

# Optimized processing paths for turning world terrain into transmitted columns.
# Compression reduces network bytes but costs CPU when a reusable frame is unavailable.
# These are expert troubleshooting switches; their effects depend on the active path.
serialization:
  selective_nbt_parse: true # New reads: parse only needed terrain data on supported raw paths.
  nbt_transcode: true # New reads: use the optimized terrain serialization path.
  compressed_columns: true # [restart] Compress columns for clients that support it.

# Allows older LOD protocol versions; these numbers are not Minecraft versions.
# Disabling a fallback restricts which clients can connect to the LOD service.
# It does not translate arbitrary modded blocks or replace a version-translation mod.
compatibility:
  protocols:
    v16: true # [restart] Accept protocol-16 clients.
    v18: true # [restart] Accept protocol-18 clients.
    v19: true # [restart] Accept protocol-19 clients.
  via_mismatch_guard: true # [restart] Guard incompatible translated-protocol sessions.

# Privacy controls for distant terrain. The x-ray settings prevent LOD data from
# revealing blocks hidden by anti-xray policy: auto follows supported detected policy,
# forcing off can expose hidden terrain, and the block list and height are fallbacks,
# not overrides for an adopted engine policy. The map-ingestion request applies on reload.
privacy:
  xray:
    mode: "auto" # [restart] "auto", "on" or "off"; auto follows detected anti-xray policy.
    max_y_blocks: 64 # [restart] Fallback mask applies below this world Y coordinate.
    hidden_blocks: # [restart] Fallback list when engine policy is unavailable; [] hides none.
      - "minecraft:copper_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_copper_ore"
      - "minecraft:raw_copper_block"
      - "minecraft:gold_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_gold_ore"
      - "minecraft:iron_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_iron_ore"
      - "minecraft:raw_iron_block"
      - "minecraft:coal_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_coal_ore"
      - "minecraft:lapis_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_lapis_ore"
      - "minecraft:mossy_cobblestone"
      - "minecraft:obsidian"
      - "minecraft:chest"
      - "minecraft:diamond_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_diamond_ore"
      - "minecraft:redstone_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_redstone_ore"
      - "minecraft:clay"
      - "minecraft:emerald_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_emerald_ore"
      - "minecraft:ender_chest"
  # Asks players' clients not to copy distant terrain into Xaero's World Map or
  # JourneyMap. Players with the lss.map_ingestion (vss.map_ingestion) permission
  # are exempt; granting it needs a permissions mod such as LuckPerms.
  # Only clients on 0.19.0 or newer can honor this, so while it is on, older
  # clients get no distant terrain (and no far players) until they update, unless
  # exempt. Clients still receive and render the terrain, so
  # a modified client can ignore the request. Maps players already saved, and
  # areas they explore normally, are not affected.
  request_no_map_ingestion: false # Ask clients not to add distant terrain to their maps.

# Sends lightweight distant-player snapshots beyond normal entity tracking range.
# This does not keep distant entities ticking. Larger ranges and more frequent
# updates can increase server work, traffic and client rendering work.
# Modes:
#   "off"      - nobody is shown.
#   "opt_in"   - only players whose own client shares their position are shown.
#   "on"       - everyone is shown, players without the mod too; a player can hide
#                with Share My Position.
#   "required" - everyone is shown and cannot opt out, except players who hold the
#                lss.farplayers.hidden (vss.farplayers.hidden) permission. A player
#                whose choice is overridden is told so once in chat.
# Exclusions, spectator and invisibility rules, vanish and disguises apply in every mode.
far_players:
  mode: "on" # "off", "opt_in", "on" (players may opt out) or "required" (only permission holders may).
  update_interval_ticks: 10 # 10 ticks = two updates/second at 20 TPS; range 2–100.
  distance:
    min_blocks: 0 # 0 = no additional inner ring; cannot exceed max_blocks.
    max_blocks: 2048 # Server visibility ceiling; range 128–16384 blocks.
  send_spectators: false # Include spectator targets if other privacy checks allow them.
  excluded_players: [] # Player names or UUIDs never shared; kept out of diagnostic exports.
  # Hide every player who holds the lss.farplayers.hidden (vss.farplayers.hidden)
  # permission, in every mode (the behaviour before 0.21.0). A grant of every
  # permission ("*") includes it, so this can hide all your admins. Off: the
  # permission hides nobody by itself; players choose with Share My Position
  # (in mode "required", only holders can).
  hide_permission_holders: false # Hide every player who holds the far-player hide permission.
```

```yaml
# LOD Server Support — Paper/Folia server defaults.
# Edit this file, then run /lsslod reload. Settings marked [restart] wait for restart.
# Reload changes policy for new work; existing jobs/reads drain and cache trimming can lag.
# Distances are radii. 1 chunk = 16 blocks; 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes.
config_version: 1 # Local settings schema version, independent of the network protocol.

# Serves distant terrain to compatible clients beyond vanilla's view distance.
# This does not increase the server's simulation distance or keep distant chunks ticking.
service:
  enabled: true # [restart] Enable the server's LOD service.
  require_permission: false # Require both lss.use and vss.use; nodes default to allowed.
  # show_permission_refusal: true # With require_permission on, a player without the permission is
  #   told "distant terrain here needs a permission you don't have". false = they see the general
  #   "switched off here". Courtesy, not secrecy: a player can compare with a friend. Remove the
  #   first "#" to set it; version 0.22 and older do not know this setting.

# Larger radii reveal more terrain, but cover more columns and can increase
# generation, transfer, cache and disk work. Doubling a radius covers roughly four
# times the area; a large configured radius does not mean it fills instantly.
lod:
  distance:
    default_chunks: 512 # Fallback for dimensions not listed below; range 1–2048, 0 = off.
    by_dimension: # Fresh-install defaults; 0 turns LODs off in that dimension.
      "minecraft:overworld": 512 # Overworld radius in chunks.
      "minecraft:the_nether": 64 # Nether radius in chunks.
      "minecraft:the_end": 512 # End radius in chunks.
    by_world: {} # Paper world-name overrides (0 = off); take priority over dimension entries.

# Lets LOD requests create terrain that does not yet exist in the world.
# This costs world-generation CPU time and grows the normal world files, independently
# of the LOD store. With generation off, existing terrain can still be served.
# Higher concurrency can fill missing terrain sooner, but competes with gameplay.
generation:
  enabled: true # Generate missing terrain; disabling stops new jobs, existing jobs finish.
  concurrency:
    global: 40 # Maximum concurrent generations across the server; range 1–512.
    per_player: 40 # Maximum per player; cannot exceed the global limit.
  timeout_ticks: 1200 # New jobs only; 60 seconds at 20 TPS, longer under lag; range 20–12000.

# Limits and schedules LOD traffic so it shares resources with normal gameplay.
# Bandwidth limits count uncompressed payload work, so they also limit client decode
# work; compressed network traffic can be much smaller. Lower limits slow terrain fill.
network:
  bandwidth:
    per_player_mib_per_second: 25 # Raw MiB/s before compression; 0 clamps to 1 KiB/s, not unlimited.
    global_mib_per_second: 75 # Shared raw MiB/s budget; 0 clamps to 1 KiB/s, not unlimited.
  send_queue_limit_per_player: 1024 # Admission ceiling; lowering it lets existing work drain.
  ping_backstop: true # Reduce LOD traffic when player latency indicates congestion.
  send_pacing: true # Spread LOD sends across ticks to reduce bursts.
  yield_to_vanilla: true # Let normal game traffic take transport priority; applies next flush.

# Keeps previously downloaded terrain up to date when the world changes.
# Shorter dirty-broadcast intervals show edits sooner but can send updates more often.
# Region summaries let returning clients validate cached areas without downloading
# every column again; they describe freshness, not the terrain itself.
updates:
  # Tick-driven: 200 ticks = 10 seconds at 20 TPS, longer under lag.
  dirty_broadcast_interval_ticks: 200 # 0 disables pushes, not invalidation; otherwise 20–6000.
  region_summaries: true # Accept new region-validation requests; accepted requests can finish.

storage:
  # Reader threads and concurrent reads control pressure on world-file access.
  # More parallel reads can improve throughput, but can also compete with gameplay
  # for disk and CPU. Automatic sizing accounts for the active read path and store.
  disk:
    reader_threads: 0 # [restart] 0 = automatic; explicit range 1–64.
    max_concurrent_reads: 0 # 0 = automatic, based on the active reader pool and store.
    background_priority: true # [restart] Use background-priority reads where supported.
    split_background_reads: true # [restart] Separate background read work where supported.
  # This RAM cache holds column freshness timestamps, not complete terrain.
  # More capacity can avoid repeated timestamp lookups, at the cost of server memory.
  # Reducing capacity trims gradually; it does not clear the entire cache on reload.
  timestamp_cache_mib_per_dimension: 0 # 0 = automatic from the largest active LOD radius.
  # Briefly remembering missing columns avoids repeatedly checking unavailable terrain.
  # A longer lifetime can delay another lookup for newly available data on a memo hit.
  miss_memo_ttl_seconds: 30 # 0 disables; maximum 60. Changing this clears old miss memos.
  # Persistent cache of prepared LOD columns, reused across players and restarts.
  # Cache hits reduce repeated world-file parsing, serialization and, when the
  # client's format supports reuse, compression. Store reads still use disk I/O.
  # Tradeoff: extra disk space and writes as terrain is cached or updated. A fully
  # warmed store can be comparable in size to the region files; actual use depends
  # on the world and how much terrain has been cached. This is rebuildable data.
  # Off still allows normal LOD serving, but loses this reuse. Disabling the store
  # does not delete its existing files or reclaim their disk space.
  lod_store:
    enabled: true # [restart] Fresh installs enable this; migration preserves old behavior.
    # Smaller limits retain less prepared terrain, so evicted columns may need
    # processing again. This bounds live database data, not total filesystem use:
    # SQLite journal files and space awaiting reclamation can add overhead.
    # Lowering the cap evicts gradually; reload does not instantly free filesystem space.
    max_size_mib: 0 # 0 = unlimited; positive range 64–1,048,576 MiB.
    # Periodically recheck saved-world freshness to catch edits without a Bukkit event.
    # Shorter intervals find these saved edits sooner but perform more checks.
    # Unsaved changes still have to reach the world files before this path can see them.
    resweep_interval_seconds: 300 # 0 disables future periodic sweeps; an active sweep can finish.

# Optimized processing paths for turning world terrain into transmitted columns.
# Compression reduces network bytes but costs CPU when a reusable frame is unavailable.
# These are expert troubleshooting switches; their effects depend on the active path.
serialization:
  selective_nbt_parse: true # Inactive on Paper's already-parsed NBT path; retained for portability.
  nbt_transcode: true # New reads: use the optimized terrain serialization path.
  compressed_columns: true # [restart] Compress columns for clients that support it.

# Allows older LOD protocol versions; these numbers are not Minecraft versions.
# Disabling a fallback restricts which clients can connect to the LOD service.
# It does not translate arbitrary modded blocks or replace a version-translation mod.
compatibility:
  protocols:
    v16: true # [restart] Accept protocol-16 clients.
    v18: true # [restart] Accept protocol-18 clients.
    v19: true # [restart] Accept protocol-19 clients.
  via_mismatch_guard: true # [restart] Guard incompatible translated-protocol sessions.

# Privacy controls for distant terrain. The x-ray settings prevent LOD data from
# revealing blocks hidden by anti-xray policy: auto follows supported detected policy,
# forcing off can expose hidden terrain, and the block list and height are fallbacks,
# not overrides for an adopted engine policy. The map-ingestion request applies on reload.
privacy:
  xray:
    mode: "auto" # [restart] "auto", "on" or "off"; auto follows detected anti-xray policy.
    max_y_blocks: 64 # [restart] Fallback mask applies below this world Y coordinate.
    hidden_blocks: # [restart] Fallback list when engine policy is unavailable; [] hides none.
      - "minecraft:copper_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_copper_ore"
      - "minecraft:raw_copper_block"
      - "minecraft:gold_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_gold_ore"
      - "minecraft:iron_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_iron_ore"
      - "minecraft:raw_iron_block"
      - "minecraft:coal_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_coal_ore"
      - "minecraft:lapis_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_lapis_ore"
      - "minecraft:mossy_cobblestone"
      - "minecraft:obsidian"
      - "minecraft:chest"
      - "minecraft:diamond_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_diamond_ore"
      - "minecraft:redstone_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_redstone_ore"
      - "minecraft:clay"
      - "minecraft:emerald_ore"
      - "minecraft:deepslate_emerald_ore"
      - "minecraft:ender_chest"
  # Asks players' clients not to copy distant terrain into Xaero's World Map or
  # JourneyMap. Players with the lss.map_ingestion (vss.map_ingestion) permission
  # are exempt; grant it with a permissions plugin such as LuckPerms.
  # Only clients on 0.19.0 or newer can honor this, so while it is on, older
  # clients get no distant terrain (and no far players) until they update, unless
  # exempt. Clients still receive and render the terrain, so
  # a modified client can ignore the request. Maps players already saved, and
  # areas they explore normally, are not affected.
  request_no_map_ingestion: false # Ask clients not to add distant terrain to their maps.

# Sends lightweight distant-player snapshots beyond normal entity tracking range.
# This does not keep distant entities ticking. Larger ranges and more frequent
# updates can increase server work, traffic and client rendering work.
# Modes:
#   "off"      - nobody is shown.
#   "opt_in"   - only players whose own client shares their position are shown.
#   "on"       - everyone is shown, players without the mod too; a player can hide
#                with Share My Position.
#   "required" - everyone is shown and cannot opt out, except players who hold the
#                lss.farplayers.hidden (vss.farplayers.hidden) permission. A player
#                whose choice is overridden is told so once in chat.
# Exclusions, spectator and invisibility rules, vanish and disguises apply in every mode.
far_players:
  mode: "on" # "off", "opt_in", "on" (players may opt out) or "required" (only permission holders may).
  update_interval_ticks: 10 # 10 ticks = two updates/second at 20 TPS; range 2–100.
  distance:
    min_blocks: 0 # 0 = no additional inner ring; cannot exceed max_blocks.
    max_blocks: 2048 # Server visibility ceiling; range 128–16384 blocks.
  send_spectators: false # Include spectator targets if other privacy checks allow them.
  excluded_players: [] # Player names or UUIDs never shared; kept out of diagnostic exports.
  # Hide every player who holds the lss.farplayers.hidden (vss.farplayers.hidden)
  # permission, in every mode (the behaviour before 0.21.0). A grant of every
  # permission ("*") includes it, so this can hide all your admins. Off: the
  # permission hides nobody by itself; players choose with Share My Position
  # (in mode "required", only holders can).
  hide_permission_holders: false # Hide every player who holds the far-player hide permission.

# Bukkit event hooks invalidate cached LODs after world edits. Adding frequent
# events can improve coverage but increase work; edits without a matching event
# may remain stale until saved terrain is checked by the store's periodic resweep.
paper:
  update_events: # [restart] Bukkit events used to detect changed terrain.
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockPlaceEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockBreakEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockExplodeEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityExplodeEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockBurnEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockFadeEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockFormEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockGrowEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockSpreadEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.LeavesDecayEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockPistonExtendEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.block.BlockPistonRetractEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityChangeBlockEvent"
    - "org.bukkit.event.world.StructureGrowEvent"
```

| integrations.xaero_map.backpressure | integrations.map_ingestion.backpressure |

The generated document includes feature explanations, resource costs and zero meanings.

```yaml
# LOD Server Support — client defaults (Fabric/NeoForge).
# After editing this file, run /lss reload to activate changes.
# Sodium Apply saves and reloads automatically. [reconnect] settings wait for the next connection.
config_version: 1 # Local settings schema version, independent of the network protocol.

# Downloads distant terrain for installed consumers such as Voxy or a map mod.
# The terrain renderer controls how that data is drawn; this download radius does
# not raise vanilla render/simulation distance. More terrain can cost client disk,
# memory and processing time. Turning reception off does not erase cached terrain.
lod:
  # Experimental keys (lod.source, lod.dh.*, lod.voxy_border_fill) are kept in the
  # separate *-client-experimental.yaml file beside this one, so this file stays
  # readable by older versions. General > Allow DH Server Terrain writes it.
  receive: true # Download server LOD terrain; off stops acquisition, not saved terrain display.
  distance_chunks: 0 # 0 = server default; otherwise 1–2048, capped by the server's radius.
  # Balance terrain fill speed against connection quality and client processing load.
  # A column-rate limit counts chunk columns, not bytes: dense/modded terrain can
  # cost more per column. Lower rates can help stutters but take longer to fill.
  # Adaptive controls react to latency or consumer backlog; they are not an FPS cap.
  download:
    max_columns_per_second: 0 # 0 = unlimited; positive range 10–100000 columns/second.
    adaptive_rate: true # Adjust download rate when latency indicates congestion; also paces DH joins.
    slow_start_on_join: true # Begin new sessions gently; requires adaptive_rate.
    ingest_backpressure: true # Slow downloads when terrain consumers fall behind.

# Controls which missing or stale terrain is requested and how often it is checked.
# Region ordering and scan shortcuts reduce repeated work; they do not invent terrain
# or increase server generation speed. These are primarily troubleshooting switches.
scan:
  region_order: true # [reconnect] Complete nearby regions instead of scanning chunk rings.
  adaptive_cadence: true # [reconnect] Rescan sooner when the current request set completes.
  retain_completed_prefix: true # [reconnect] Avoid rewalking already satisfied terrain.
  quadtree: true # [reconnect] Use the optimized completed-region scan.
  region_summaries: true # [reconnect] Validate cached terrain using server summaries.

# Tracks terrain freshness so revisits can avoid downloading unchanged columns.
# This is separate from the terrain renderer's own saved data. World separation
# prevents one server address's replacement world from inheriting stale freshness.
# Use address aliases only for addresses reaching the same world, with matching
# consumer storage; sharing freshness alone could leave missing terrain unrequested.
cache:
  split_by_world: true # [reconnect] Separate cache identity when one address changes worlds.
  address_aliases: [] # [reconnect] Ordered address groups; first address is canonical.
  # Example: [["play.example.com", "alt.example.com"]]. Requires consumer corroboration.
  # Aliases stay inactive while map ingestion writes into a per-server map store.

# Protocol fallbacks allow older LOD servers. Block fallbacks provide a local visual
# substitute when this client does not know a received block; they do not install
# missing content or make otherwise incompatible modpacks compatible.
compatibility:
  protocols:
    v16: true # [reconnect] Allow fallback to protocol-16 servers.
    v19: true # [reconnect] Allow fallback to protocol-19 servers.
  v16_generation: true # [reconnect] Request generation from compatible protocol-16 servers.
  block_fallbacks:
    default: "minecraft:stone" # [reconnect] Unknown block fallback; must not resolve to air.
    overrides: {} # [reconnect] Remote block ID -> local block ID mappings.

integrations:
  # Writes received distant terrain into installed map mods (Xaero's World Map, JourneyMap),
  # so the map shows beyond the area you have explored. See the README for supported versions.
  # Maps save these tiles like explored terrain (they stay until you revisit), and a large LOD
  # distance can add GBs of map data. Map writing paces downloads so maps stay complete; turning
  # this off stops future writes after reconnect without removing terrain already saved.
  # map_ingestion.nether_store_mib (experimental file, default 256) caps the disk kept to fill
  # Xaero's cave layers when you switch layer; 0 = no store and no fill on switch.
  map_ingestion:
    enabled: true # [reconnect] Write server terrain into installed map mods; off = maps show only explored terrain.
    backpressure: true # Pace downloads to map writes; requires ingest_backpressure.

# Draws distant player models from server snapshots, not fully simulated entities.
# Larger render/animation distances add client work; reducing animation distance
# keeps distant models visible while skipping their walk animation.
# Showing other players and sharing your own position are independent choices:
# disabling this renderer does not automatically hide you from other players.
far_players:
  enabled: true # Show distant players when this loader has a renderer and the server allows it.
  distance:
    min_blocks: 0 # 0 = server-controlled inner ring; otherwise up to 16384 blocks.
    max_blocks: 0 # 0 = server maximum; otherwise up to 16384 blocks.
  name_tags: true # Show this mod's far-player name tags.
  full_bright: false # Draw distant players at full brightness, including at night.
  render_distance_blocks: 0 # 0 = effective server/client ring; caps models and name tags.
  # extend_far_plane (experimental file, default true) draws far players past the game's
  # far clipping plane, out to the farthest far player; it only acts while an LOD mod such
  # as Voxy is drawing, and not while a shader pack is on. Fog can still hide very distant players:
  # turn off your LOD mod's fog if they fade out.
  animation_distance_blocks: 512 # Animate nearby proxies; 0 = no walk animation.
  # Controls whether others may see your position through the far-player feature.
  # This does not hide you from normal Minecraft tracking or unrelated systems.
  # Sodium Apply activates this choice; after a disk edit, run /lss reload.
  sharing:
    enabled: true # Let other players see you at a distance; use Sodium Apply or /lss reload.
    max_distance_blocks: 0 # 0 = no extra sharing cap; otherwise up to 16384 blocks.
```

A missing store key in legacy JSON migrates to store disabled; fresh YAML enables it.
Legacy generation and dirty-broadcast seconds are normalized under their old bounds
then converted to tick counts. Private aliases and exclusion lists are not diagnostic
exports. Client position sharing remains independent from local far-player rendering.

Use `tools/settings/settings_file.py` for harness creation, validation, migration and
atomic edits. It calls the same Java schema, parser and persistence implementation as
the product. A successful edit still needs the appropriate reload command and receipt.
